title: Effects of Napping in Sleep-Restricted Adolescents
brief_summary: To examine the neurobehavioural responses to two successive cycles of sleep restriction and recovery in adolescents, and to determine the benefits of napping on cognitive performance, alertness, and mood. 57 participants, aged 15 to 19 years old, were divided into nap and no-nap groups. Both groups underwent two cycles of sleep restriction and recovery over 15 days. The nap group received an afternoon sleep opportunity lasting 1 hour.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* healthy
* no sleep disorder
* body mass index not greater than 30

Exclusion Criteria:

* smoker
* habitual short sleeper (time in bed during term time of less than 6 hours and no sign of sleep extension of greater than 1 hour on weekends)
* consumption of more than 5 cups of caffeinated beverages a day
* travelling across more than 2 time zones in the month prior to the study protocol
* diagnosed with any psychiatric conditions
